catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extracted from Continuous Architecture System (CAS) runner codebase, governance schemas, and steering documentation.
analysis_limits: Dynamic agent run logs and remote LiteLLM endpoints not directly executed during static analysis
Analysis scoped to Python runner (src/cas_runner), markdown architecture flows, and template schemas

system_map.overview: The Continuous Architecture System (CAS) operates as a multi-tier governance harness for autonomous agents. It coordinates agent execution via FlowRunner, steers agent behaviour using synthesized prompt facts from git deltas, and validates architectural compliance through deterministic state machines and compliance engines.

agents.name: AgenticMerger
agents.role: Reconciles incoming git architectural changes and knowledge artifacts with canonical governance repositories.

agents.name: ComplianceEngine
agents.role: Evaluates project codebases and pull requests against declarative architectural rules, emitting structured compliance findings.

agents.name: GovernanceActionEngine
agents.role: Executes stateful transitions, approvals, and exception handoffs within a controlled finite state machine.

orchestration.description: FlowRunner executes sequential and event-triggered pipeline steps using pre-calculated steering indices, combining deterministic FSM validation with agentic LLM synthesis.

tools_and_integrations.name: LiteLLMClient
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Provides unified access to downstream LLM inference providers with deterministic retry and token budgeting.

tools_and_integrations.name: OpenTelemetry SDK
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Emits trace spans and execution metrics across agent decision loops.

tools_and_integrations.name: SteeringRuntimeIndex
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Aggregates capabilities, lineage records, and prompt facts into a queryable memory structure.

state_and_memory.description: Git-backed knowledge repository containing decisions, models, patterns, rules, and runtime profiles.
Steering indices computed from raw git diffs and capability lineages, materialized into prompt facts.
FlowRunner step execution context and transient LiteLLM completion traces.

patterns.name: Steering Projection and Prompt Fact Synthesis

tool_protocols.notes: Generates structured context injected into agent system prompts.

optimisation_targets.notes: Compresses vast architectural lineage into high-density prompt facts.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Guides autonomy within tight boundary facts rather than unrestricted exploration.

patterns.summary: Compiles raw architectural deltas and capability lineages into compact, typed PromptFact objects for LLM context steering.
patterns.intent: Prevent LLM architectural drift without overloading context windows with redundant history.
patterns.context: Used during pull request evaluation and workflow runs in CAS runner before invoking agentic synthesis.
forces: Repository history is too large to fit in raw LLM context
Agents make poor design decisions when unguided by domain rules
Rules must update dynamically as code matures
patterns.solution: Extract capability changes into typed RawGitDelta and CapabilityLineage objects, compiling them into a SteeringRuntimeIndex that projects compact PromptFacts.

evidence.note: Defines typed entities that distill git changes into structured steerable context.

benefits: Deterministic, explainable context injection
Prevents token bloat from raw commit histories
Standardized prompt grounding across models
costs: Requires maintenance of capability lineage extractors
Static extraction may miss subtle semantic diffs
failure_modes: Lineage extractor misinterprets breaking change, producing contradictory prompt facts.

patterns.reuse_notes: Extract repository changes to domain models into typed summary records, converting them to prompt bullet points before LLM calls.

patterns.name: Deterministic Governance Action State Machine

tool_protocols.notes: Actions are executed within strict state machine transitions.

optimisation_targets.notes: Prevents unauthorized state transitions or illegal operational actions.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Actions are gated by a hardcoded transition registry.

patterns.summary: Restricts agent modifications to governance state through an explicit TransitionRegistry FSM.
patterns.intent: Ensure agents cannot bypass approval gates, skip compliance checks, or trigger arbitrary state mutations.
patterns.context: Governs lifecycle operations such as promotion decisions, rule exceptions, and architecture approvals.
forces: Autonomous agents can hallucinate or attempt illegal state changes
Auditability demands deterministic proof of valid transitions
patterns.solution: Define TransitionRegistry verifying (current_state, proposed_action) tuples before applying mutations in GovernanceActionEngine.
implementation_signals: GovernanceAction model with typed action kinds and targets

evidence.note: Validates state transitions prior to executing governance actions.
Typed models enforcing action definitions and error handling.

benefits: Zero tolerance for illegal transition paths
Audit trail guarantees compliance status validity
Isolates decision planning from state mutation
costs: State transition map must be updated whenever lifecycle rules evolve
failure_modes: Engine blocks benign workflow when transition table lacks an edge case.

patterns.reuse_notes: Pair any agentic action execution with an in-process FSM table verifying origin and target states before execution.

patterns.name: Workspace Governance Context Injection

tool_protocols.notes: Writes static governance steering directly into agent config files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md).

optimisation_targets.notes: Synchronizes runtime instruction rules with coding agent instruction files.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Pins system boundary instructions into files read automatically by coding assistants.

patterns.summary: Injects canonical governance blocks into developer assistant entrypoints (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md) at workspace bootstrap.
patterns.intent: Harmonize agent behaviors across third-party IDE agents and CLI tools without relying solely on centralized runtime wrappers.
patterns.context: Runs during bootstrap initialization when setting up or synchronizing client repos.
forces: Different agent tools read disparate markdown instruction files
Maintaining consistency across AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and GEMINI.md manually causes drift
patterns.solution: A central bootstrap utility reads the canonical governance policy and merges marked blocks into target workspace markdown files.
implementation_signals: Delimited markdown blocks with CAS anchors

evidence.note: Replaces or inserts demarcated governance sections into agent markdown files.

benefits: Consistent guidelines across Claude, Gemini, and custom agents
Idempotent updates on re-running bootstrap
Developer-visible steering rules stored in source control
costs: Risk of merge collisions if users manually alter demarcated blocks
failure_modes: Broken anchor markers cause accidental duplication or partial truncation of instruction files.

patterns.reuse_notes: Use demarcated delimiter comments in system instructions to update agent guidelines idempotently during CI or repository setup.

patterns.name: Model-Agnostic LLM Facade with Mock Fallback

tool_protocols.notes: Standardized abstraction wrapping LiteLLM API and offline Mock client.

optimisation_targets.notes: Decouples business and governance logic from specific model vendor APIs.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Hides provider-specific prompt schemas and networking.

patterns.summary: Abstracts multi-vendor LLM invocation behind a unified interface with a deterministic mock fallback for offline and CI testing.
patterns.intent: Allow agent flows to run seamlessly in local dev, offline CI, and cloud environments without vendor lock-in.
patterns.context: Underlies all LLM-powered components in cas_runner including AgenticMerger and synthesis steps.
forces: Direct vendor SDK dependencies create vendor lock-in and test fragility
Automated CI testing cannot make costly or flaky external API calls
patterns.solution: Wrap LiteLLM inside LiteLLMClient implementing a common call interface, paired with MockLLMClient that returns canned or synthesized responses.
implementation_signals: MockLLMClient returning deterministic outputs without network calls

evidence.note: Mock client enabling deterministic zero-cost unit and flow testing.

benefits: Zero network overhead during unit tests
Portability between OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, and local models
Predictable cost control and timeout handling
costs: Mock client may drift from real LLM response nuances
failure_modes: Production client experiences unhandled provider rate limit while mock tests pass silently.

patterns.reuse_notes: Implement a common protocol for LLM calls with constructor injection of Mock vs Production clients across all orchestration steps.

patterns.name: Declarative Schema-Enforced Compliance Evaluation

tool_protocols.notes: Enforces typed output models for compliance evaluations.

optimisation_targets.notes: Guarantees evaluation results are machine-readable and unambiguous.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Evaluation outcomes must strictly conform to Pydantic models.

patterns.summary: Validates runtime decisions and code changes against rule schemas, producing strongly-typed ComplianceFinding objects.
patterns.intent: Prevent subjective or ambiguous LLM evaluation outputs by constraining compliance metrics to strictly validated schemas.
patterns.context: Invoked during CI/CD checks and CAS runner compliance reviews against rule-context.json.
forces: Unstructured LLM reviews cannot trigger automated gating in CI/CD pipelines
Compliance checks must provide explicit severities, file references, and remediation steps
patterns.solution: Define declarative Pydantic schemas (ComplianceFinding, ComplianceMetrics) that the ComplianceEngine parses and validates against target repository artifacts.
implementation_signals: ComplianceFinding Pydantic schema with rule IDs and severity levels

evidence.note: Typed models defining findings, severities, and metrics.

benefits: Deterministic gate passes in CI/CD based on metric thresholds
Actionable remediation metadata for developer consumption
Protection against schema drift
costs: Rules must be explicitly modeled and catalogued before automated evaluation
failure_modes: Pydantic validation failure when an LLM agent produces non-conforming finding structures.

patterns.reuse_notes: Define strict Pydantic models for evaluation outputs, rejecting or re-prompting evaluations that fail validation.

patterns.name: Agentic Reconciliation and Knowledge Synthesis

tool_protocols.notes: Performs diff-based merging and resolves knowledge conflicts.

optimisation_targets.notes: Synthesizes parallel repository knowledge changes without manual conflict resolution.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: LLM reconciles semantic conflicts that standard git three-way merges cannot resolve.

patterns.summary: Employs an LLM-powered AgenticMerger to synthesize conflicting knowledge artifacts and git deltas into a coherent governance inventory.
patterns.intent: Resolve semantic divergences in architecture documentation, decision records, and pattern definitions across multiple feature branches.
patterns.context: Executes when synchronizing project architectural records back into cas-knowledge global stores.
forces: Textual git merge conflicts break architectural markdown formatting
Different agents may independently add overlapping architectural rules or patterns
patterns.solution: Pass conflicting delta objects and existing inventory to AgenticMerger, which leverages LLM reasoning to output a deduplicated ResolutionResult.
implementation_signals: ResolutionResult model returning resolved contents and conflicts

evidence.note: Data structures representing reconciliation outputs and stored inventory.

benefits: Automatic resolution of semantic documentation overlaps
Preserves structural integrity of markdown ADRs and pattern files
Reduces manual PR review burden on architects
costs: Inference cost on large documentation sets
Requires validation checks against hallucinated deletions
failure_modes: LLM accidentally summarizes away critical edge-case warnings during document synthesis.

patterns.reuse_notes: Use LLM synthesis specifically for unstructured or semi-structured documentation conflicts where git 3-way merge is too brittle.

patterns.name: Sequential Flow Pipeline Runner

tool_protocols.notes: Executes coordinated pipeline steps passing context downstream.

optimisation_targets.notes: Provides deterministic step sequencing with explicit error aborts.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Predictable, auditable pipeline flow over autonomous agent looping.

patterns.summary: Orchestrates multi-phase architecture workflows through a structured FlowRunner coordinating setup, extraction, evaluation, and reporting.
patterns.intent: Maintain deterministic execution order across extraction, compliance validation, and dashboard rendering.
patterns.context: Main execution engine instantiated from src/cas_runner/cli.py to run local and CI tasks.
forces: Complex workflows risk inconsistent state if agent tasks execute out of order
Failures at early stages (e.g. git diff extraction) must abort before calling LLM APIs
patterns.solution: Encapsulate pipeline execution within FlowRunner, which chains discrete steps and passes shared execution context between them.

evidence.note: Dispatches user CLI arguments to the runner.

benefits: Clear failure boundaries and step isolation
Predictable context propagation
Straightforward debugging and step-level profiling
costs: Less dynamic than a purely autonomous agent deciding its own next tool calls
failure_modes: Cascading failures when an upstream step returns corrupt data that passes schema check.

patterns.reuse_notes: Implement sequential pipeline runners for multi-step tasks where strict phase ordering is required before invoking agentic synthesis.

patterns.name: Telemetry-Grounded Health Observability

tool_protocols.notes: Captures execution traces and metric models to compute operational health.

optimisation_targets.notes: Provides transparency into agent decision stability and system health.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Deterministic health calculations over opaque agent self-reporting.

patterns.summary: Computes composite governance health status and diagnostics by aggregating OpenTelemetry execution spans and traceable compliance metrics.
patterns.intent: Detect degradation in architectural compliance, error rates, or agent execution throughput over time.
patterns.context: Used in dashboard generation and health calculation routines in src/cas_runner/dashboard.
forces: Silent drift in agent reasoning can compromise codebase quality without raising exceptions
Decision makers need an aggregated health indicator rather than thousands of raw trace events
patterns.solution: Define TraceableMetric and HealthStatus models; compute weighted health using calculate_health() and get_health_reasons() over runtime traces.
implementation_signals: TraceableMetric in models.py with timestamp and trace id

evidence.note: Calculates categorical health status from risk indicators.
Encapsulates metric payloads with trace attribution.

benefits: Early warning system for governance decay and agent regression
Trace attribution connects health dips to specific pipeline runs
Actionable diagnostics through get_health_reasons
costs: Requires consistent metric instrumentation across all agent steps
failure_modes: Misconfigured metric weights produce false-positive alerts, causing alert fatigue.

patterns.reuse_notes: Tag all agent execution outputs with trace identifiers and compute an aggregated health score to gate PR merges or deployments.

patterns.name: Template-Driven Artifact Evolution

tool_protocols.notes: Agents populate structured markdown schemas for decisions and patterns.

optimisation_targets.notes: Standardizes artifact outputs for downstream consumption and cataloguing.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents write freeform reasoning within strictly formatted markdown sections.

patterns.summary: Constrains agent knowledge generation using standardized markdown templates spanning heuristics, signals, patterns, and decisions.
patterns.intent: Ensure architectural knowledge produced by agents conforms to standard section headers, lifecycle statuses, and metadata keys.
patterns.context: cas-knowledge repository templates utilized by agents to capture learnings, ADRs, and patterns.
forces: Freeform markdown generated by LLMs lacks consistent headings for automated parsing
Architects require standard fields (Intent, Context, Forces, Solution) to review proposals
patterns.solution: Provide canonical markdown templates with fixed headers and YAML frontmatter; enforce agents to instantiate these templates when recording discoveries.
implementation_signals: Promotion templates from heuristic to pattern
Structured headers in pattern and ADR templates

evidence.note: Canonical schema for capturing architectural patterns.
Lifecycle promotion template documenting transition criteria.

benefits: Consistent documentation structure across human and agent authors
Facilitates automated parsing by static analysis scripts
Encourages thorough reasoning by forcing consideration of forces and failure modes
costs: Template updates require backward-compatibility checks across existing knowledge base
failure_modes: Agents fill required sections with filler text or tautological statements to satisfy templates.

patterns.reuse_notes: Ground agent text generation tasks by providing explicit template skeletons containing required header tags and expected semantics.

anti_patterns.name: Unbounded Knowledge State Drift
symptoms: Project-specific rules contradict global enterprise decisions
Agent decisions repeatedly flag false positives in compliance scans
Templates in project subdirectories diverge from cas-knowledge/templates/

where_observed.note: Documents the requirement for continuous synchronization loops between project and global tiers.

impact: Agents generate non-compliant code based on outdated local rules, requiring human intervention to revert.
suggested_remediation: Schedule continuous automated sync workflows (.github/workflows/cas-managed-steering-sync.yml) to reconcile local project knowledge with the global baseline.

anti_patterns.name: Bypassing State Machine Transition Registry
symptoms: GovernanceAction models applied directly to inventory without calling TransitionRegistry.validate_transition
Actions transitioning directly from proposed to approved without intermediate compliance review

where_observed.note: Guards against unvalidated transitions by throwing GovernanceException.

impact: Breaches governance integrity by allowing automated agents to approve their own exceptions or pattern promotions.
suggested_remediation: Ensure all mutations route strictly through GovernanceActionService which enforces TransitionRegistry checks before persistence.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Compact prompt facts compiled deterministically from typed git deltas and capability indices rather than feeding raw commit logs into LLMs.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Establishes a repeatable, typed boundary between repository state and agent prompt context.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: OpenTelemetry spans coupled with structured TraceableMetric payloads and aggregate health scoring models.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Enables end-to-end tracing across pipeline phases and automated health dashboarding.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Rule context schemas validated by ComplianceEngine emitting typed ComplianceFinding records with explicit severities.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Prevents unstructured or vague LLM feedback in CI pipelines.

open_questions.question: How are concurrent multi-branch reconciliation conflicts handled in AgenticMerger when two agents update the global knowledge base simultaneously?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Simultaneous pull requests could result in race conditions or lost updates in cas-knowledge global maps.
open_questions.evidence_gap: Static code exhibits sequential reconciliation; lock semantics or distributed merging hooks are not evident.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Examine GitHub Actions workflow definitions (.github/workflows/cas-continuous-architecture.yml) for concurrency group settings.
